--- New conversation turns ---
Hannah: I propose adding a dynamic "safety envelope" that monitors real-time outputs and overrides the AI if it violates predefined physical or ethical boundaries. This adds a layer of runtime protection and requires investment in a separate, simpler monitoring system, but it ensures safety even if the primary AI encounters an unforeseen state.
Richard: We should integrate "graceful degradation" protocols that transition the system to a minimal risk state when uncertainty thresholds are exceeded. This requires investment in redundant hardware and fail-safe logic, but prevents catastrophic failure when the safety envelope is triggered.
Maria: I propose mandatory adversarial "red teaming" to intentionally stress-test the system against malicious inputs or unexpected environmental noise. This necessitates a budget for external security audits and simulation environments, but it identifies vulnerabilities that internal safety envelopes might overlook.

Hannah: I propose integrating an interpretability layer that provides human-readable justifications for high-stakes decisions in real-time.
